For patients with mild hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh score 5-6), fosamprenavir should be administered at a dose of 700 mg orally every 12 hours without ritonavir in therapy-naïve patients. Alternatively, 700 mg every 12 hours with ritonavir 100 mg once daily can be used for therapy-naïve or protease inhibitor-experienced patients. 2. For patients with moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh score 7-9), fosamprenavir should be administered at a dose of 700 mg orally every 12 hours without ritonavir in therapy-naïve patients. Alternatively, 450 mg every 12 hours with ritonavir 100 mg once daily can be used for therapy-naïve or protease inhibitor-experienced patients. 3. For patients with severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh score 10-15), fosamprenavir should be administered at a dose of 350 mg orally every 12 hours without ritonavir in therapy-naïve patients. Alternatively, 300 mg every 12 hours with ritonavir 100 mg once daily can be used for therapy-naïve or protease inhibitor-experienced patients. 4. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of alfuzosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of conivaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Conivaptan should not be co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 7. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine (oral or intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 8. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of eliglustat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are contraindicated in poor or intermediate metabolizers of eliglustat. For extensive metabolizers, reduce the eliglustat dose from 84 mg twice daily to 84 mg once daily. Eliglustat is contraindicated if strong or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors are used concomitantly with strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 9. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be co-administered with other antiretrovirals. Etravirine increases fosamprenavir levels by decreasing its metabolism, and this combination is contraindicated. 10. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Co-administration of flibanserin with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. 11. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of irinotecan (including liposomal formulations) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 12. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of ivabradine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Co-administration of ivabradine with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 13. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of lomitapide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of significantly increased lomitapide levels. 14. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 15. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of lovastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the increased risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 16. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of lurasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Co-administration of lurasidone with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 17. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of naloxegol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors can significantly increase naloxegol systemic exposure, potentially precipitating opioid withdrawal symptoms. 18. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of pimozide by inhibiting its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of QT interval prolongation. 19. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of regorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase regorafenib levels and decrease exposure to its active metabolites (M-2 and M-5). 20. Rifampin decreases fosamprenavir levels by increasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as it may result in loss of antiviral efficacy and/or development of viral resistance. 21. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of salmeterol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the potential for increased toxicity. 22. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of simvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the increased risk of rhabdomyolysis. 23. St. John’s Wort decreases fosamprenavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 24. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated during the initial ramp-up dosing phase of venetoclax. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used after the ramp-up phase, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 75%. 25. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If short-term use of a strong CYP3A inhibitor is necessary (e.g., up to 7 days), temporarily interrupt acalabrutinib treatment. 26. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of ado-trastuzumab emtansine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors as they may increase DM1 (the cytotoxic component) exposure and toxicity. 27. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of amiodarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 28. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of amitriptyline and amoxapine by inhibiting their metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 29. Apalutamide decreases fosamprenavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, with CYP3A4 substrates can result in lower exposure to these medications. 30. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of atorvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit atorvastatin dose to 20 mg/day. 31. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of avanafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug due to the risk of severe adverse events, including hypotension, syncope, visual changes, and priapism. 32. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the avapritinib starting dose. 33. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of axitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the axitinib dose by 50%. 34. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of bedaquiline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors for more than 14 consecutive days unless the benefit outweighs the risk. 35. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of ceritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration if possible. If unavoidable, reduce the ceritinib dose by approximately 33%. 36. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of colchicine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid use of colchicine with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, especially in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 37. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of copanlisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the copanlisib dose to 45 mg. 38. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of dabrafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 39. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of desipramine, dosulepin, and doxepin by inhibiting their metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 40. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of dronedarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 41. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of elacestrant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 42. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of encorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose. 43. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of entrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 44. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of ergoloid mesylates and ergotamine by inhibiting their metabolism. This combination is contraindicated.
